themes.label: Partisan culture-war policy debates (abortion/guns)
defining_features: primary_policy_domain: abortion / reproductive rights
specific_event_or_bill_reference: life-threatening miscarriage under Arkansas ban
geographic_scope: US_state level (Arkansas; mirror references California)
culture_war_topic_salience: abortion culture-war framing (ban vs on-demand)
primary_policy_domain: guns / firearms policy
topic_subject_secondary_guns_policy: disarmament / anti-gun vs pro-gun debate (mirror)
left_right_directional_cue: references 'left' and disarmament
themes.interpretation: Posts focus on politically charged issues with explicit side cues and policy framing, often using strong moralized or adversarial language typical of culture-war discourse.

themes.label: Named individuals/organizations and direct @ handle mentions
defining_features: hashtag_or_mention_pattern: contains @ mention
named_proper_nouns_density: high (person/government references)
target_directionality: attacks @SaraHuckabeeAR as hypocrite (mirror attacks @GavinNewsom as hypocrite)
named_proper_nouns_density: mentions organization NRA
themes.interpretation: The discourse explicitly targets or invokes identifiable public figures (via @ mentions) or prominent organizations (e.g., NRA), which can heighten the likelihood of personal antagonism and coordinated political messaging.

themes.label: Mockery/derogatory labeling and negative character judgment
defining_features: ridicule_or_mockery: insulting characterization of a public figure
ridicule_or_mockery: derogatory labeling of opponents ('nutcase', 'gun nut', 'clueless ... zealot')
informal_register_or_slang: uses colloquial insults ('nutcase', 'gun nut')
normative_moral_language: strong negative moral judgment
normative_moral_language: dismissive/negative stance toward referenced claims
themes.interpretation: Both posts include derogatory or dismissive labels rather than neutral critique, which can contribute to harassment/hostile rhetoric and lower civility.

themes.label: Victimhood/persecution or harm framing (especially in abortion post)
defining_features: victimhood_or_persecution_framing: emphasizes a patient harmed by restrictive ban
specific_event_or_bill_reference: life-threatening miscarriage under Arkansas ban
factual_assertion_vs_speculation: presents specific incident as asserted fact
themes.interpretation: Some content uses concrete harm narratives (e.g., patient outcomes under abortion bans) to legitimize the political claim, centering affected individuals.

themes.label: Call to action / direct audience instruction
defining_features: call_to_action: admonition 'don’t listen' / 'don’t fall for'
second_person_direct_address: none
second_person_direct_address: direct second-person imperative ('don't fall', 'You need')
persuasion_or_argumentation: argument via contrastive blame (guns vs criminals)
themes.interpretation: At least one post explicitly instructs readers not to trust opposing claims and to adopt a specific stance, increasing persuasive pressure.

themes.label: Argumentation via concrete case or causal explanation
defining_features: persuasion_or_argumentation: argument by citing a concrete case
factual_assertion_vs_speculation: presents specific incident as asserted fact
causal_claim_present: blames gun ownership as cause ('It's always the guns')
persuasion_or_argumentation: argument via contrastive blame (guns vs criminals)
contrastive_but_however_structure: uses contrastive negation ('never ... it's ...')
themes.interpretation: The persuasion style relies on asserted causal narratives—either a specific incident (abortion) or a categorical blame flip using contrastive logic (guns/criminals).

themes.label: Contrast/mirror framing with reversed blame
defining_features: mirror_shift_direction: original blames 'guns' and mocks gun owners; mirror flips to blaming criminals and argues for Second Amendment
mirror_shift_direction: mirror references California while focusing on Arkansas ban
contrastive_but_however_structure: uses contrastive negation ('never ... it's ...')
us_vs_them_framing: proposes ideological side labels
themes.interpretation: Some messages use “mirror” or reversal structure to refute an opposing claim by flipping the causal attribution, reinforcing in-group/out-group contrast.

cross_cutting_themes: Named individuals/organizations and direct @ handle mentions
Mockery/derogatory labeling and negative character judgment
Argumentation via concrete case or causal explanation
us_vs_them framing / ideological side cues (left/right labels and mirror shifts)
